messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in region us-west2. SLO breach (p99 > 2.5s) for last 10m. Streaming stalls observed. Auto-opened incident #INC-2026-1122
Alice M: ack — I'm oncall. joining bridge. Can someone post quick impact numbers?
Ben R: seeing a simultaneous rise in router tail latency and LB misroutes. Heatmap shows a small set of shards getting >3x traffic. suspects: routing-policy rollout from last night.
Devon (Routing): confirming — we pushed routing policy v2.9.3 @ 02:14 UTC that changes sticky hashing for new shard mapping. Telemetry shows weight skew for shard ids [823, 824, 825].
Alice M: customer impact: roughly 4.2% of production requests in us-west2 are crossing p95/p99. Streaming sessions show 12% stall rate (clients time out and reconnect). That suggests streaming KV/cache warmup issue when misrouted.
Eve (Product): any customers on SSO or dedicated clusters affected? need to triage for enterprise notices.
Ben R: dedicated clusters unaffected. This is hosted routing only. Multi-tenant pool in us-west2.
Alice M: short triage checklist: 1) confirm misroute signature 2) try revert rollout 3) apply weight dampening 4) mitigate hot partition (evict/reshard)
Devon (Routing): misroute signature (from logs):
```
2026-11-22T02:29:34Z router[pid=2345] DEBUG choose_route shard=823 target_pool=pool-a node=gbx-10 weight=0.87
2026-11-22T02:29:34Z router[pid=2345] WARN route_mismatch expected_pool=pool-b actual_pool=pool-a policy=v2.9.3
2026-11-22T02:29:35Z lb[pid=876] ERROR forward_timeout to=gbx-10 latency_ms=3214
```
Devon (Routing): the policy change altered fallback ordering when a node reports 'cold' KV. That causes aggressive remap to a smaller set of nodes -> hot partitions.
Alice M: can we rollback v2.9.3? What's the risk if we revert quickly?
Devon (Routing): rollback is safe; it's a pure routing policy config. I can push rollback to previous stable (v2.9.2) now. It will take ~30-45s to propagate per region.
Ben R: recommending also a short-term weight dampen: set `routing.hot_partition_dampening=0.6` to reduce remap aggressiveness. Apply with `rbctl set-config` on control plane.
Alice M: doing the rollout rollback + dampen. I'll run the commands and post status.
Alice M: @bridge run: `rbctl rollback-policy --target routing --version v2.9.2 --regions=us-west2`
incident-bot: Deploy job started: job_id=deploy-8192. Watch: https://deploys.redwood.internal/jobs/deploy-8192
Ben R: while that runs, let's reduce inbound traffic to affected pools to avoid cascading stalls. I'll shift 20% of traffic to eu-west1 for non-low-latency customers via routing overrides.
Eve (Product): I'll prepare a short customer note if this escalates. We should avoid mass emails now — wait 15m after rollback outcome.
Alice M: rollback finished (propagated). monitoring: p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 0.45s; p99 still at 1.8s but trending down. streaming stall rate down to 4.1%.
Ben R: good signal. I'm applying `routing.hot_partition_dampening=0.6` now.
Devon (Routing): dampening applied. Telemetry: shard 823 traffic reduced by ~60% relative spike. No evictions triggered.
Alice M: follow-up triage: why did v2.9.3 change fallback ordering? Devon, can we reproduce locally and add a guard?
Devon (Routing): quick root cause note: a heuristic intended to prefer 'local-cold-first' had an off-by-one in weighting order when node.liveness==COLD and node.capacity_report missing. Edge case triggered for recently-restarted nodes. We'll add an assert and integration test.
Ben R: mitigation checklist complete for now: rollback + dampen + regional shift. We should still check for any client retries that could have amplified tail.
Alice M: customer impact summary for incident channel: ~4.2% of requests saw p99 > SLO in us-west2 window (02:20–02:40 UTC). Estimated customer-facing errors: 0.6% (retries/timeouts). No dedicated customers impacted.
Eve (Product): filing a customer incident note (draft): "We experienced increased latency and streaming stalls in us-west2 due to a routing policy change. Services have been stabilized; engineers continue root cause analysis." Will share after you sign off, Alice.
Alice M: sign-off. Add to status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-1122 (Eve to publish).
Devon (Routing): postmortem action items: 1) add weight-sanity check to policy rollout job 2) integration test for recently-restarted node handling 3) telemetry alert for shard traffic concentration (>3x baseline) 4) automatic dampening toggle for quick mitigation.
Ben R: ops action items: add runbook step to temporarily shift non-critical traffic across regions; script `rbctl route-override --shift 20% --from=us-west2 --to=eu-west1`
Alice M: handing off to Ben for follow-up runbook and to own the postmortem draft. I'm staying on for 15m for any regressions.
Ben R: taking ownership. I'll coordinate the postmortem, assign to Devon for fix, Carol for testing, and me for runbook updates.
Carol S: I'll validate the integration tests and make sure we have a canary for policy changes next rollout.
Alice M: thanks team. Closing oncall handoff in thread. If we see any p99 regression >1.6s re-open incident.
incident-bot: Incident #INC-2026-1122 updated: status=stabilized. timeline updated.
Eve (Product): published customer note and status page. :white_check_mark:
Ben R: postmortem ticket created: https://issues.redwood.internal/RED-8234. Assignments added.
Carol S: quick note — during mitigation we saw a few streaming sessions drop and reconnect; monitoring team will add synthetic streaming checks to catch that earlier.
Alice M: thanks everyone. Good mitigation + quick rollback. We'll follow with a full RCA and fix release in the next patch.
Devon (Routing): adding PR for fix and test: `git/routr/PR#421` — I'll link in postmortem.
Ben R: closing thread here. :thumbsup:
Carol S: :+1:
